The best short games on PS Plus

Not every great game asks for 100 hours. These are our ten favourite games on PS Plus that you can finish in a weekend or less, from a two-hour story to a tough-but-fair platformer. Each one says roughly how long it takes, based on HowLongToBeat's averages, so you can fit one into the time you have. The full list of games under 10 hours follows.

What counts as short

A game counts as short here if HowLongToBeat's players finish its main story in under 10 hours on average. That's the time to see the credits at a normal pace, not to find every collectible, so completionists should expect longer.

Games without an ending, like most multiplayer, sports and endless games, aren't counted, because there's no story to finish. Our picks lean towards games that feel complete rather than cut short.

1

Celeste

PS4 · Metascore 91 · 99% recommend on OpenCritic · about 8.3 h main story

Madeline sets out to climb Celeste Mountain, and you guide her through hundreds of tight, inventive platforming screens. It's hard but always fair, with instant restarts and an Assist Mode if you need it. Underneath the jumping is a warm, honest story about anxiety and self-doubt.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

2

Undertale

PS4 · Metascore 92 · 97% recommend on OpenCritic · about 7 h main story

A small RPG with a big reputation. You fall into an underground world of monsters, and you can talk your way out of every fight instead of winning it. It's funny, strange and surprisingly moving, and the choices you make change how it all plays out.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

3

Shadow of the Colossus

PS4 · Metascore 91 · about 7.2 h main story

A lone hero rides across a vast, empty land to topple sixteen giant colossi, each one a living puzzle you have to climb. This is Bluepoint's beautiful PS4 remake of the PS2 classic, and it still has one of the most haunting endings in games.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

4

Sword of the Sea

PS5 · Metascore 88 · about 2.7 h main story

From the makers of Abzû and Journey's art director: you surf across sweeping desert dunes on a hovering sword, bringing a lost sea back to life as you go. It's pure, flowing movement with gorgeous art and music, and you'll want to play it again right away.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

5

Neva

PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 87 · about 4.1 h main story

A young woman named Alba and a wolf cub named Neva travel together through a dying, painterly world over the course of the seasons. It's from the team behind GRIS, mixing gentle platforming with tense fights and a wordless story about growing up.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

6

Indika

PS5 · Metascore 80 · about 4.1 h main story

Indika is a young nun in a strange, alternate 19th-century Russia, and the Devil himself is a voice in her head. Sent on an errand across a frozen landscape, she falls in with an escaped convict, and what follows is a darkly funny, often surreal story about faith and doubt. It's like nothing else on the service.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

7

Hotline Miami

PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 85 · about 5.2 h main story

A brutal, neon-soaked top-down action game set in 1989 Miami, where you clear out buildings in a single blur of violence and die in one hit. Its pounding synth soundtrack and "one more try" loop make it hard to put down. Very violent, so not one for the kids.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

8

GRIS

PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 82 · about 3.5 h main story

A wordless journey through a watercolour world that slowly gains colour as a young woman works through her grief. There's no way to fail, just gentle platforming, stunning art and music. Perfect for a quiet evening.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

9

Venba

PS5 · Metascore 79 · about 1.5 h main story

A short, heartfelt story about an Indian family who move to Canada in the 1980s, told through cooking. You piece together the mother's recipes from a smudged old cookbook, and each dish carries a memory. You can finish it in one sitting.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

10

Bramble: The Mountain King

PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 80 · about 4.7 h main story

A young boy follows his sister into a forest straight out of Nordic folklore, where the fairy-tale creatures are anything but friendly. It begins beautiful and turns very dark, with some genuinely grim moments and memorable boss fights, so it's one for older players.

Questions

What's the best short game on PS Plus?

Celeste and Undertale are two of the highest-rated games on the whole service, and both take under 10 hours. For something you can finish in an evening, Sword of the Sea takes about 3 hours.

What can I finish in one sitting?

Venba takes about an hour and a half, and Sword of the Sea, GRIS and Indika each take around 3 to 4 hours.

Where do the times come from?

They're HowLongToBeat's averages for finishing the main story. Your own time will vary, especially in tougher games like Celeste.

What are good short games for a beginner?

GRIS has no way to fail, and Venba is a relaxed story about cooking. Celeste is tough, but its Assist Mode lets anyone see it through.

Are there short horror games on PS Plus?

Yes. Bramble: The Mountain King is on this list, and Crow Country takes around 5 hours too. Our horror list has more.

How do I find more short games?

The full list below covers every game on PS Plus under 10 hours. On the wall, you can filter by length and hide what you've already played.
